literal: Even at the moment of seeing him who does not love, thinking 'he will not be angry', you go, my heart.
translation: O my heart! Even when you see him who does not show love, you still go to him, thinking that he will not be angry with you.
modern: என்னிடம் அன்பு காட்டாதவரைப் பார்த்த போதிலும், 'அவர் கோபப்பட மாட்டார்' என்று நினைத்து அவரிடம் செல்கிறாயே, என் நெஞ்சமே!
explanation: In this couplet, the heroine addresses her own heart, which is eager to reunite with her distant lover. She points out the irony that even though he does not show affection ('uṟāatavar'), her heart immediately rushes to him the moment he is seen ('kaṇṭa kaṇṇum'). The heart foolishly reassures itself that he will not be angry or cold ('ceṟāar ena'). This portrays the helpless nature of love, where the heart ignores past indifference and remains ever-optimistic about the beloved.
